reasoning: Both models reviewed the critical files (PKGBUILD, .SRCINFO) and found them to be standard AUR packaging for a -bin package. The package downloads pre-built binaries from the project's own Codeberg repository with pinned SHA256 checksums. No malicious code execution, no fetching from unrelated hosts, no injection patterns detected. The first model's 'inconclusive' verdict was due to API errors on non-critical files (.gitignore, .nvchecker.toml), not security concerns.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement is not about security but tool reliability. The qwen model encountered HTTP 400 errors when reviewing .gitignore and .nvchecker.toml, forcing an 'inconclusive' overall verdict. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and correctly identified them as safe. Both models agreed on the security assessment of the critical files (PKGBUILD, .SRCINFO).
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review .gitignore and .nvchecker.toml due to API errors (HTTP 400 BadRequestError)
learnings: API errors on non-executable configuration files (.gitignore, .nvchecker.toml) should not force an 'inconclusive' security verdict when critical files (PKGBUILD, .SRCINFO) have been successfully reviewed and found safe
The audit tool should distinguish between 'inconclusive due to tool errors' and 'inconclusive due to security concerns' - tool errors should be reported separately and not block a final verdict
Non-executable metadata files should be deprioritized in coverage requirements when they cannot affect makepkg execution
